title: Choose the portfolio's direction
question: Five opening screens, each built in real code from your own projects. Keep the lead, take another, or re-roll. Three more dealt worlds wait in the re-roll pool.

options.label: Network Map
options.thesis: Four projects drawn as four transit lines that meet at the skills they share.
options.viewport: A full network map: your name on a station sign, four lines crossing at JavaScript, SQL and layered architecture.
options.risk: Skill subway maps are a known infographic idea, and project screens stay hidden until a station is opened.

raised.raise: The map answers the pointer: focus one line and the other three dim.
Unbuilt work is drawn as deliberately as built work: planned features appear as dashed stops.
The network prints line by line in a fixed order on load, with the key arriving last.

options.label: Solved by A*
options.lineage: the sliding 8-puzzle from your own Pathfinder-8
options.thesis: The home page is a sliding puzzle whose tiles are the site, solved live by your own search algorithm.
options.viewport: Your name on the left and a 3 by 3 board on the right; eight tiles are the sections, and A* slides them home on load.
options.risk: Playful interactive heroes are familiar on developer portfolios, and a puzzle delays reading unless it solves itself fast.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: Each project is an instruction step: the parts it is made of, exploded and clicked together.
options.viewport: Step 1 fills the page: SkolarTrack as a React brick over an Express brick on a PostgreSQL baseplate, beside a parts inventory.
options.case: Beats the map on both counts: everyone knows the booklet, and it shows what each project is made of.
options.risk: Toy grammar can read as a children's product unless the type and keylines stay strict.

options.label: Series One
options.lineage: numbered insert cards and their albums
options.thesis: A numbered card set: four printed, four empty slots, each card flipping to a dense spec on its back.
options.viewport: An album page of eight slots, four filled with project cards and one already flipped to its back.
options.case: Holds clarity, since a card back is exactly the spec a client checks, but loses on identification.
options.risk: Reads hobbyist, and the empty slots put what is missing on show.

options.label: Ink Basin
options.thesis: The page as a basin of marbled ink that the pointer stirs.
options.viewport: One continuous fluid surface with text held to a still margin.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a marbled surface says nothing about what you build.
options.kept: A surface that answers the pointer.
options.risk: A fluid simulation would claim graphics skills your projects do not show.

canonCard.label: The Awwwards standard
canonCard.thesis: The monochrome, type-led portfolio that wins Site of the Day, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: A project index in large type, a preview image following the cursor, and your full name across the bottom.
canonCard.risk: Looks like many other portfolios by design.
